creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-10-28 on rad v0.12.1, still so on 2026-10-29. The one-line script `a, b = 1, 2` runs, and `rad check` on it prints "No diagnostics to report", but `rad fmt` prints `<file>: could not parse, skipping.` and leaves the file unformatted. The same assignment inside a `fn` body formats fine, as does `a, b = [1, 2]` at top level.

The message names no line and no parse error, so in a longer script the only way to find the cause was bisecting the file by hand.

Related: a_2o8ewx9Sm, another case of rad check and rad fmt disagreeing about a script.

Possibly: make rad fmt's parser accept a top-level multi-value assignment, and have "could not parse" print the line and the parse error.
title: rad fmt cannot parse a top-level multi-value assignment that rad runs and rad check passes
